topic: Matrimonial Stream Triage — FJSS Pro Bono & Modest Means
user_query: Applicant has a family or matrimonial matter (divorce, custody, maintenance, family violence). How do I triage this?
variations: Applicant wants to file for divorce.
Applicant is a foreigner married to a Singaporean.
Applicant has a Syariah divorce matter.
Applicant needs a lawyer for family court.
part_a_general_info: Reached from GEN3-T01 Route H. The Matrimonial Stream covers divorce (civil and Syariah), custody, care & control, maintenance, variation of court orders, and family violence applications (Personal Protection Orders). The two PBSG representation schemes here are FJSS (Pro Bono) and FJSS (Modest Means). FJSS (Pro Bono) eligibility: • Applicant is a foreigner with at least one Singaporean child (the child must be below 21). • Applicant faces matrimonial legal issue (including Syariah divorce, custody, maintenance, variation) covered by FJSS (if unsure, check with PBSG Staff). • Applicant meets means test (https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation/), financial documents will need to be submitted upon application. • Applicant passes merits test (legal assessment on whether the case warrants representation, this will be done after application is submitted, intern/volunteer taking triaging call is NOT to reject based on their own assessment, no matter how unmeritorious the case appears to be). FJSS (Modest Means) eligibility: • Applicant is a Singapore Citizen / PR who has marginally failed the Legal Aid Bureau's means test, OR a foreigner with at least one Singaporean child, who has marginally failed FJSS (Pro Bono)'s means test. • Applicant faces matrimonial legal issue (including Syariah divorce, custody, maintenance, variation) covered by FJSS (if unsure, check with PBSG Staff). • Applicant meets means test (https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation/), financial documents will need to be submitted upon application. • Applicant passes merits test (legal assessment on whether the case warrants representation, this will be done after application is submitted, intern/volunteer taking triaging call is NOT to reject based on their own assessment, no matter how unmeritorious the case appears to be).
triage_questions: Q1: Is there active or recent family violence (against the applicant or a child), or is there court date/deadline within 14 days?
Q2: Is the applicant a Singapore Citizen or PR?
Q3 (SGC/PR path): Has the applicant applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) for civil legal aid?
Q4 (Foreigner path): Does the applicant have at least one Singaporean child (under 21)?

Q5 (Means): Is the applicant's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$1,050, does the applicant have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the applicant stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?

Q1.question: Is there active or recent family violence (against the applicant or a child), or is there court date/deadline within 14 days?
Q1.if_yes: Route A (FJSS + Urgent concurrent — cross-reference GEN3-T06)

Q2.question: Is the applicant a Singapore Citizen or PR?
Q2.if_no_foreigner: Proceed to Q4 (FJSS Pro Bono pathway)
Q2.if_not_sure: Clarify nationality/residency status; if still unclear, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).

Q3.question: (SGC/PR path) Has the applicant applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) for civil legal aid?
Q3.if_yes_passed_or_processing: Route C (LAB is handling — PBSG not needed)
Q3.if_yes_failed_means_test: Proceed to Q5 (FJSS Modest Means path)
Q3.if_not_sure: Route B for applicant to check application status with LAB.

Q4.question: (Foreigner path) Does the applicant have at least one Singaporean child (under 21)?
Q4.if_no: Proceed to GEN3-T04 — Civil and Guidance Stream Triage
Q4.if_not_sure: Clarify whether the applicant has at least one child who is a Singapore Citizen and is below 21 years old (Q2 already established the applicant is not SGC/PR); if still unclear, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).

Q5.question: (Means) Is the applicant's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$1,050, does the applicant have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the applicant stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?
Q5.pchi_definition: PCHI = total monthly household income ÷ number of persons in household, including the applicant and all dependants.
Q5.if_yes: Route D (FJSS Pro Bono — Standard Intake)
Q5.if_no_marginal: Route E (FJSS Modest Means). Marginal thresholds: PCHI ≤ S$1,400, savings ≤ $12,000 if younger than 60 (or ≤ $48,000 if 60+), non-private housing.
Q5.if_no_well_over: Proceed to GEN3-T04 — Civil and Guidance Stream Triage
Q5.if_not_sure: Walk through the thresholds; if still unclear, take down figures and proceed to Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).

routing: Route A (FJSS + Urgent Concurrent): Proceed to GEN3-T06, following which, regardless of triage outcome of GEN3-T06, proceed to Q2 of GEN3-T03. Present both triaging outcomes to applicant.

Route B (Refer to LAB First): Describe the Legal Aid Bureau for civil/family matters: "LAB is the government's legal aid office for low-income SGC/PR facing civil and family proceedings. As you are a Singapore Citizen/PR, you should apply to LAB first. These are their eligibility criteria: https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/legal-services/do-i-qualify/ and https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/legal-services/taking-the-means-test/. If LAB is unable to assist and you are unable to afford paid legal services, you can come back to us with your LAB rejection letter/reasons for us to assess whether we are able to assist. If you are able to afford a lawyer, we are unfortunately not likely able to assist but can provide you with directories of lawyers and some self-help resources for your consideration.” Provide LAB contact: https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/ | 1800 2255 529 | appointment needed (through their website/hotline) for visit at 45 Maxwell Road #07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118. Resources to share with the applicant: SupportGoWhere — social and financial assistance PBSG YouTube channel — webinars on common legal issues Singapore Legal Advice — directory of lawyers and legal advice over the phone for a small fee Law Society of Singapore — directory of lawyers Legal Services Regulatory Authority e-Services — search for lawyers by practice area Caveat (share with applicant): "These are third-party websites not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG. We share them as general pointers only and cannot vouch for the service, fees, or outcomes. If you have any questions on these services, please reach out to them directly."

Route C (LAB is Handling): Inform the applicant that they should direct any queries on their ongoing LAB application to LAB. Provide LAB contact: https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/ | 1800 2255 529 | appointment needed (through their website/hotline) for visit at 45 Maxwell Road #07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118. Resources to share with the applicant: SupportGoWhere — social and financial assistance PBSG YouTube channel — webinars on common legal issues Singapore Legal Advice — directory of lawyers and legal advice over the phone for a small fee Law Society of Singapore — directory of lawyers Legal Services Regulatory Authority e-Services — search for lawyers by practice area Caveat (share with applicant): "These are third-party websites not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG. We share them as general pointers only and cannot vouch for the service, fees, or outcomes. If you have any questions on these services, please reach out to them directly."

Route D (FJSS Pro Bono — Standard Intake): Share about FJSS Pro Bono (GEN3-I04 — Information Card — FJSS (Pro Bono)) and inform applicant that they may be eligible. Inform applicant to apply for FJSS: https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation. If applicant is unable to self-apply, inform applicant to go to PBSG Counter at State Courts Help Centre (1 Havelock Square, #B1-18 State Courts, Singapore 059724) with documents needed. If applicant has difficulties going to PBSG, proceed to Route F.

Route E (FJSS Modest Means — Standard Intake): Share about FJSS Modest Means (GEN3-I05 — Information Card — FJSS (Modest Means)) and inform applicant that they may be eligible. Inform applicant to apply for FJSS: https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation. If applicant is unable to self-apply, inform applicant to go to PBSG Counter at State Courts Help Centre (1 Havelock Square, #B1-18 State Courts, Singapore 059724) with documents needed. If applicant has difficulties going to PBSG, proceed to Route F.

Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff): Take down: full name, contact number, email (if any), brief matter description including answers to Q1-Q5, any urgency/vulnerability factors noted. Inform the applicant that PBSG Staff will call back within 1–2 working days. Email information to PBSG Staff on the same day. Do NOT attempt to advise further.

Route A.name: FJSS + Urgent Concurrent
Route A.script: Your family matter may also involve urgency, such as violence or a deadline. I need to check the urgent issue first, then I will continue the FJSS questions after that.
needs_to_know: GEN3-T06 urgent triage must be completed before continuing to GEN3-T03 Q2.
The urgent route and matrimonial stream outcome should both be presented where applicable.
prepare: Any family violence or safety concerns
intern_steps: Proceed to GEN3-T06 Q1 before asking GEN3-T03 Q2.
After the urgent leg is complete, resume GEN3-T03 at Q2.
Present both the urgent triage outcome and matrimonial stream outcome where applicable.
caveats: Do not let GEN3-T06's standalone return-to-GEN3-T01 wording override the parent resume point.

Route B.name: Refer to LAB First
Route B.script: Because you are a Singapore Citizen or PR facing a family or matrimonial matter, you should apply to the Legal Aid Bureau first. LAB is the government's legal aid office for low-income Singapore Citizens and PRs facing civil and family proceedings. If LAB is unable to assist and you cannot afford paid legal services, you can come back to PBSG with your LAB rejection letter or reasons so we can assess whether we may be able to help.
needs_to_know: LAB should be the first port of call for eligible Singapore Citizens or PRs seeking family or civil representation.
If the applicant can afford a lawyer, PBSG is not likely able to assist but can share lawyer directories and self-help resources.
access: Address: 45 Maxwell Road #07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
Opening hours / appointment instructions: Appointment needed through LAB's website or hotline
prepare: LAB rejection letter or reasons, if LAB is unable to assist
Financial documents for LAB's means test
intern_steps: Share LAB's website, eligibility criteria, means test information, phone number, and appointment instructions.
If the applicant later receives a LAB rejection or reasons, tell them they may return to PBSG for assessment.
caveats: Third-party resources are general pointers only and are not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG.

Route C.name: LAB is Handling
Route C.script: Because LAB is already handling your application, you should direct questions about that application to LAB. I can share LAB's contact details with you.
needs_to_know: PBSG is not needed while LAB is handling or processing the application.
access: Address: 45 Maxwell Road #07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
Opening hours / appointment instructions: Appointment needed through LAB's website or hotline
prepare: LAB application reference or correspondence, if any
intern_steps: Do not advise on the ongoing LAB application.
caveats: Third-party resources are general pointers only and are not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG.

Route D.name: FJSS Pro Bono — Standard Intake
Route D.script: You may be eligible for FJSS Pro Bono. Please apply through Pro Bono SG's legal representation application page. If you cannot self-apply, you may go to the PBSG Counter at the State Courts Help Centre with the required documents.
needs_to_know: FJSS Pro Bono is a Pro Bono SG representation scheme for eligible matrimonial matters.
access: Address: 1 Havelock Square, #B1-18 State Courts, Singapore 059724
prepare: Financial documents for the means test
Matrimonial matter details and supporting documents if asked on application
intern_steps: Share the FJSS application link with the applicant.
If the applicant cannot self-apply, direct them to the PBSG Counter.
If there are difficulties going to PBSG, escalate to PBSG Staff.
caveats: Do not give legal advice or assess merits yourself.

Route E.name: FJSS Modest Means — Standard Intake
Route E.script: You may be eligible for FJSS Modest Means. Please apply through Pro Bono SG's legal representation application page. If you cannot self-apply, you may go to the PBSG Counter at the State Courts Help Centre with the required documents.
needs_to_know: FJSS Modest Means is a low-cost Pro Bono SG representation pathway for eligible matrimonial matters.
access: Address: 1 Havelock Square, #B1-18 State Courts, Singapore 059724
prepare: Financial documents for the means test
Matrimonial matter details and supporting documents if asked on application
intern_steps: Share the FJSS application link with the applicant.
If the applicant cannot self-apply, direct them to the PBSG Counter.
If there are difficulties going to PBSG, escalate to PBSG Staff.
caveats: Do not give legal advice or assess merits yourself.

Route F.name: Escalate to PBSG Staff
Route F.script: I need to check this with PBSG Staff before going further. Let me collect your details and have PBSG Staff follow up.
needs_to_know: PBSG Staff will call back within 1-2 working days.
intern_steps: Take down the applicant's full name, contact number, email if any, and brief matter description.
Include answers to Q1-Q5 and any urgency or vulnerability factors noted.
Email the information to PBSG Staff on the same day.
Do not attempt to advise further.
caveats: Do not give legal advice or assess merits yourself.

guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the applicant; (b) apply the law to the applicant's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the applicant what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the applicant insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect applicant confidentiality. Do not discuss the applicant outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
